rejected.title: Ideas, concerns and tensions
card: Idea
a big concept a text explores, such as belonging, power or freedom. It is usually named in a word or short phrase.
Concern
something the text seems worried about or wants readers to think about, such as how a community treats outsiders.
Tension
a clash between people, groups or values, such as loyalty to family against a wish for independence. Tensions often drive what happens.
To find them, ask what the characters want, what stands in their way, and which values pull in different directions.
rejected.remember: A text explores ideas and concerns, and clashes between people or values often drive what happens.

a.q: In a novel, Priya wants to leave her small town for university, but her parents need her to run the family shop. Which is the tension?
opts: Her ambition pulls against her family's needs
The story is set in a quiet small town
Priya enjoys studying and wants good marks
The family shop is one of the novel's settings
a.why: A tension is a clash between people or values. Priya's wish to leave pulls against what her parents need from her. The small town and the shop are only details of setting and show no clash.
a.clue: Look for two things pulling against each other.

b.q: A short story shows a new student, Tomas, eating alone while other students laugh together. Which idea does this scene most clearly explore?
opts: Belonging and being left out
Power and the control of others
Freedom and the wish to travel
Memory and the passing of time
b.why: The scene shows Tomas apart from a group that is close, which points to belonging. Power is a tempting answer, but nothing shows anyone controlling anyone else.
b.clue: Ask whether Tomas is inside or outside the group.

a.q: In a novel, Priya wants to leave her small town for university, but her parents need her to run the family shop. Which is the tension?
opts: Her own ambitions clash with duty to her family
The story is set in a small town
Priya is a student who likes to study
The novel has a shop as one of its settings
a.why: A tension is a clash between people or values. Priya's wish to leave pulls against her family's needs. The setting is only a detail and does not show a clash.
a.clue: Look for two things pulling against each other.

b.q: A short story shows a new student, Tomas, eating alone while other students laugh together. Which idea does this scene most clearly explore?
opts: Belonging and being left out
Power and the control of others
Freedom and the wish to travel
Memory and the passing of time
b.why: The scene shows Tomas separate from a group that is close, which points to belonging. Power is a tempting answer, but nothing shows anyone controlling anyone else.
b.clue: Ask whether Tomas is inside or outside the group.

a.best: Her own ambitions clash with duty to her family
